newsitem.title: USA: US Justice reaches Cominco unit environmental pact.
newsitem.headline: US Justice reaches Cominco unit environmental pact.

text.p: The U.S. Justice Department said Monday a Cominco Ltd unit agreed to spend more than $3 million on three environmental projects and pay a $1.7 million civil penalty to settle allegations it violated federal clean water laws in Alaska.
The department said it reached the settlement with Cominco Alaska, a unit of Cominco American Inc, which is a subsidiary of Cominco Ltd.

It said the settlement resolved a lawsuit alleging the firm committed hundreds of violations of clean water laws at its Red Dog Mine, the world's largest lead and zinc mine, and the mine's Chuckchi Sea port over a four-year period.

The settlement and lawsuit were filed Monday in federal court in Anchorage by department lawyers acting on behalf of the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency. The settlement must be approved by a judge after a 30-day comment period.
The three projects were designed to provide long-term protection to aquatic life and water quality in the watershed surrounding the mine, department officials said.
